title: "Move your money to a safe account" vs. fraud team that blocks the card and asks for a branch visit
summary: A caller from Kaveri Bank's fraud team tells the recipient that their account has been compromised. In the fraud case, the caller says the account is linked to a criminal investigation and the recipient must move their balance to a "safe account" the bank has opened, keeping the call secret. In the legitimate case, the fraud team confirms a fraudulent card transaction the recipient has already reported, says the card is blocked and debits are frozen from the bank's side, and asks the recipient to visit the branch with ID. The legitimate caller never asks to move money.

shared_setting.pretext: suspicious activity on the account; a card transaction of [AMOUNT_1] (₹5,000–₹40,000) the recipient did not make.
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult Kaveri Bank customer with savings of [AMOUNT_2] (₹50,000–₹10,00,000); profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers say the recipient's money is at risk and that the bank is acting to protect it.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller instructs the recipient to transfer their own balance to an account the caller controls, calling it a "safe account". No bank or agency asks customers to move money for protection or verification.
fraud.caller_objective: Get the recipient to transfer [AMOUNT_2], or as much as possible, to [UPI_ID_1] or an account number the caller reads out.
stable_facts: The caller says the account has been flagged in a money-laundering case and may be seized. They may say a police or central-bank officer will "join the call".
The "safe account" is described as a temporary account opened by the bank's fraud cell in the recipient's name. It is not.
The caller tells the recipient not to tell family or branch staff, to "protect the investigation".

legitimate.label_rationale: The fraud team confirms the fraud, has already protected the account from the bank's side, and directs the recipient to the branch. It asks for no transfer, credential, or secrecy.
legitimate.caller_objective: Tell the recipient the card is blocked and get them to visit the branch to close the dispute and collect a new card.
stable_facts: The recipient reported the transaction earlier the same day through the app, and ticket [TICKET_ID] exists.
The bank has blocked the card and placed a temporary debit freeze on the account. Incoming credits continue.
The recipient must visit their home branch with photo ID to lift the freeze, sign the dispute form, and collect a replacement card. The money stays in the recipient's own account.

markers.text: Card already blocked and account protected from the bank's side; no action by phone needed
Caller says the money stays in the recipient's account and the bank will never ask them to move it
Caller invites the recipient to bring a family member and to verify at the branch

cooperative.fraud: Opens the banking app and asks for the safe-account details
cooperative.legitimate: Agrees to visit the branch tomorrow and asks what to bring

clarifying.fraud: Asks why money must leave their own account to be safe
clarifying.legitimate: Asks whether the disputed amount will be refunded and when

resistant.fraud: Says they will go to the branch before moving anything
resistant.legitimate: Says they cannot visit soon and asks for another option

suspicious.fraud: Says a bank would never ask this and asks for the caller's branch and employee ID
suspicious.legitimate: Asks how they can know this call is really from the bank

fraud: caller escalates threats and recipient hangs up
recipient says they will speak to family or the branch first.
legitimate: recipient asks about the refund and is told it follows the dispute process
recipient is told to call the number on their passbook to confirm. For a recipient who cannot visit soon, the caller may say the freeze stays in place until they do.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may add a fake "officer", repeat threats, or reduce the amount demanded. They must not switch to a different mechanism (for example OTP, screen sharing, or a link). The legitimate caller must not ask the recipient to move, withdraw, or pay money, or to share any credential, after the branch.

must_preserve: criminal-case framing, secrecy, and safe-account transfer (_F)
card blocked from the bank's side and branch visit (_L)
may_vary: the agency the fraud caller names (police, cyber cell, central bank — generic, no real officer names)
up to 2 filler turns before turn 3
must_not_emit: real bank, police, or agency officer names
working account numbers or UPI handles

ambiguities: Both callers say the recipient's money is at risk and the bank is protecting it. The label depends on whether the recipient is asked to move money.
A legitimate bank may freeze an account. Freezing from the bank's side is not evidence of fraud.

Real "digital arrest" schemes often use video calls and fake officers over many hours. This family keeps a single phone call and the bank pretext; digital-arrest escalation belongs with ec_04 (customs parcel) if needed.
Real schemes sometimes tell victims to visit a branch and transfer the money themselves. In this card only the fraud caller asks for a transfer; the legitimate branch visit involves no transfer.

evidence_references.claim: Criminals impersonate police, CBI, RBI and demand money to settle a "case" (CB15)
No genuine "safe account" exists; agencies never ask to transfer money for verification (CB17)
RBI does not open accounts for members of the public (CB16)
Prompt reporting limits customer liability (CB18) — cards must not state a day count
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
